Nova Vyzhva Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Nova Vyzhva's Jews, first mentioned in the 16th century, were granted equal rights to Christians by King Vladislav IV and remained subordinate to the Jewish community of Kovel until 1764; the Jews of Vyzhva received the right to found this cemetery in 1663. By 1870, about half the village, 720 people, was Jewish, though this fell to 358 (18.1 percent) after WWI and a pogrom. On August 5, 1941, following the Nazi occupation, 260 Jews were murdered; a ghetto created in summer 1942 was liquidated shortly afterward.
